impact:
CORRECTED 2026-08-31 after checking history — the original framing ("decide whether onboarding is part of the product") was wrong and would have led to deleting a working feature.

onboard was never REPLACED by setup. It was never wired up at all.

EVIDENCE:
- src/onboard.ts is real and complete: 126 lines, an interactive 5-question flow that seeds PERSONA.md, added by T-009 (061b038).
- `git log --all --oneline -S'"onboard"' -- src/cli.ts` returns NOTHING. The CLI command dispatch has never contained an `onboard` case on any branch in the project's history. There was no removal to find.
- Its only local imports are ./api-key.js and ./storage.js, both already in the published files allowlist. It would work today if wired.
- It is reachable only via the repo-local pnpm script "onboard": "tsx src/onboard.ts" — unavailable to anyone who installed from npm.

THREE SURFACES PROMISE THE COMMAND:
1. README.md:136 — "zug onboard    Seed your cognitive fingerprint (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY optional, improves output)". Added by T-034 (e1f1a5e), which first shipped in v1.0.4. The README has therefore documented a nonexistent command across five releases, including 1.3.0 published today.
2. src/setup.ts (~212) — "✓ Zug: created PERSONA.md — run 'zug onboard' to seed your cognitive fingerprint", added by T-033.
3. src/cli.ts (~83) — "No PERSONA.md found. Run 'pnpm onboard' to create one." — a repo-local pnpm script surfacing in a globally installed binary.

Actual CLI command set: --version, archive, backup, compact, persona, pull, push, resume, setup, status, sync, tail, update, version.

FIRST-RUN IMPACT: install 1.3.0 -> `zug setup` -> told to run `zug onboard` -> unknown command -> README confirms the command they just failed to run. This is the opening experience of the published OSS package and, later, of paying users.

CORRECTED FIX DIRECTION: wire it up rather than remove the references. Three independent surfaces promise it and the implementation exists and works, so intent is not ambiguous. Add an `onboard` case to the cli.ts dispatch that invokes the flow, add "dist/onboard.js" to package.json files, and change cli.ts:83 to say `zug onboard` rather than `pnpm onboard`. Verify by installing the packed tarball into a scratch prefix and running the command, the same way the version-check defect was verified.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE CLASS: the files allowlist and the CLI dispatch are both maintained by hand with nothing checking them against each other, the README, or the actual require graph. The sibling defect (dist/version-check.js required by cli.js but omitted from files, fixed in e3983ec) came from the same gap and would have shipped a dead binary. A test that (a) resolves published entrypoints' imports against the files allowlist and (b) asserts every command named in README's table exists in the dispatch would catch both.
title: `zug onboard` is documented and prompted in three places but was never wired into the CLI
